runs.t: Fault tolerance lets a system continue delivering acceptable behavior when components fail. It combines redundancy, isolation, graceful degradation, recovery and explicit fault assumptions.

Define which failures to tolerate: instance crash, zone loss, timeout, bad data or dependency unavailability. Use health checks, queues, bulkheads, bounded retries and recovery drills tied to actual business priorities.
A booking service continues accepting reservation searches when email is down, queues receipts for later and prevents email failure from undoing confirmed reservations.
Redundant replicas sharing one database or cloud zone may share the same failure mode. Graceful degradation must never compromise payment correctness or access control.
